posts.text: EIGHT GIGAWATTS ON A SINGLE SITE. THAT IS THE PITCH THE NUCLEAR COMPANY IS BRINGING TO WASHINGTON NEXT MONTH. THE GIGAWATT AGE · The Nuclear Company is planning nuclear campuses of two to four gigawatts per site, with a stated pathway to six to eight gigawatts per site, deployed as fleets rather than one-off projects. · The company argues that fleet-scale nuclear requires an entirely new technology stack to design, license, construct, and operate, which it brands Nuclear OS. · The pitch goes public September 8 in Washington, DC, with a Nuclear OS screening and live demos as part of Deep Tech Week. Most of the oxygen over the past two years has gone to reactors measured in tens or hundreds of megawatts. This is the counter-thesis, and it says the binding constraint was never reactor size but construction repeatability. The May 2026 Brookfield joint venture, built exclusively around Westinghouse AP1000 and AP300 and named project manager for V.C. Summer, is what gives that thesis something real to point at. $CCJ $BAM If the bottleneck was never the reactor, what have we actually been optimizing for? Planning to be in the room September 8, barring the unforeseen.
